title: Triumph by Caryl Churchill at The Public #annaleighashford #carylchur...
transcript: In the shortest play I have ever seen, a surprising amount of ground is covered. Starring real-life couple Annaleigh Ashford and Joe Tapper, this free pop-up production at The Public is about a woman named Iris who develops a severe case of cognitive dissonance as press secretary to the Roman emperors. Annaleigh Ashford is great, and she develops the character more deeply than you'd expect from such a short piece, though the messaging here isn't exactly subtle. When you only have 20 minutes, you have to cut to the chase. The piece is premiering concurrently in London, so I'm curious about the impression it makes over there. Monarchy is everywhere, but Iris feels uncannily similar to another blonde and steadfast press secretary in the States. Overall, this piece feels more like a sketch from a journal entry than anything else, or a political comic strip on stage. And like a comic, I don't know how memorable it'll be, but it provides a cheap thrill, in the figurative and literal sense.
